title: Eymerich's Directorium Inquisitorum: Magic Categorized as Heresy
description: Nicolau Eymerich, Inquisitor General of Aragon, completed his Directorium Inquisitorum in 1376, the most comprehensive inquisitor's manual of the medieval period. Eymerich's treatise explicitly categorized invocation of demons as heresy rather than mere superstition, arguing that any ritual invoking or honoring a demon constituted an act of apostasy. His systematic treatment of magic within the heresy framework provided inquisitors with both the legal authority and the theological justification to prosecute magic users under heresy procedure — including torture. The Directorium became a standard reference, revised and republished by Francisco Peña in 1578, and remained influential well into the early modern period.
historiographical_note: Edward Peters's The Magician, the Witch, and the Law (1978) traced how Eymerich's theoretical framework for prosecuting magic as heresy was elaborated by subsequent inquisitors. The Directorium represents the point at which the extension of inquisitorial jurisdiction to magic had been fully theorized — creating the legal basis for the prosecutions of the following centuries.
source_method: Eymerich, Directorium Inquisitorum (1376; Peña edition 1578); secondary scholarship on inquisitorial law
